notes.definition: Higher tier, separate Biology: plant growth hormones are used in agriculture and horticulture. Auxins are used as weed killers, rooting powders and to promote growth in tissue culture; ethene controls the ripening of fruit; gibberellins end seed dormancy, promote flowering and increase fruit size.
explanation: Because plant hormones control growth, people can use them, or synthetic versions of them, to control how crops grow. This is useful in agriculture (farming) and horticulture (growing fruit, vegetables and flowers). You need to describe the effects of some plant hormones and the different ways people use them.

Auxins are used as selective weed killers. Synthetic auxins sprayed on a field are absorbed in large amounts by broad-leaved weeds, which then grow rapidly and uncontrollably and die. Narrow-leaved crops such as wheat and other cereals absorb less and are not affected. With fewer weeds there is less competition for light, water and mineral ions, so the crop yield increases.

Auxins are also used as rooting powders. The cut end of a plant cutting is dipped in rooting powder containing auxin, which makes roots grow quickly. Gardeners and growers can produce many identical plants (clones) from one parent plant with desirable features. Auxins are also used to promote growth in tissue culture, where small pieces of plant tissue are grown on a nutrient medium to produce many clones.

Ethene is used in the food industry to control the ripening of fruit during storage and transport. Fruit such as bananas can be picked while unripe and firm, so it is less easily damaged. It is kept cool with low ethene levels to slow ripening, then exposed to ethene gas in a ripening room shortly before it goes on sale. This means fruit is ripe when customers want it and less is wasted.

Gibberellins can be used to end seed dormancy, so seeds germinate when growers want them to, all at the same time. For example, brewers use gibberellins to make barley seeds germinate for malting. Gibberellins can also promote flowering, so plants flower even when conditions would not normally trigger it, and increase fruit size, for example in seedless grapes.

keyTerms.definition: A synthetic auxin that kills broad-leaved weeds, by causing rapid uncontrolled growth, without harming narrow-leaved crops.
A powder containing auxin that makes cuttings develop roots quickly.
Growing new plants from small groups of cells on a nutrient medium; auxins promote their growth.
A period when a seed is alive but does not germinate; gibberellins can end it.
Changes that make fruit soft, sweet and ready to eat; controlled by ethene.
The growing of fruit, vegetables and ornamental plants.
A piece of stem cut from a plant that can grow into a new, genetically identical plant.

workedExamples.title: Percentage increase in yield
workedExamples.question: Spraying a wheat field with selective weed killer increased the yield from 6.4 to 8.0 tonnes per hectare. Calculate the percentage increase.

workedExamples.title: Scaling a dilution
workedExamples.question: Instructions say to mix 20 cm³ of weed killer concentrate with 4 dm³ of water. How much concentrate is needed for 30 dm³ of water?
steps: Concentrate per dm³ of water = 20 ÷ 4 = 5 cm³ per dm³

workedExamples.title: Comparing success with rooting powder
workedExamples.question: 34 of 40 cuttings dipped in rooting powder grew roots, compared with 18 of 40 untreated cuttings. Compare the percentages.
workedExamples.answer: Rooting powder raised the success rate from 45 % to 85 %, because auxin stimulates root growth.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think selective weed killers poison weeds by stopping photosynthesis.
misconceptions.right: In fact they are synthetic auxins that cause broad-leaved weeds to grow rapidly and uncontrollably, so the weeds die.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think ethene is used to make fruit grow bigger.
misconceptions.right: In fact ethene controls ripening. Gibberellins are used to increase fruit size.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think rooting powder contains fertiliser.
misconceptions.right: In fact rooting powder contains auxin, a plant hormone, which stimulates roots to grow from the cutting.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think gibberellins are used to ripen fruit.
misconceptions.right: In fact gibberellins end seed dormancy, promote flowering and increase fruit size; ripening is controlled by ethene.

realWorld: Bananas are shipped green from tropical countries and ripened with ethene in ripening rooms in the UK before going to supermarkets.
Brewers treat barley with gibberellins to make all the grains germinate together during malting.
Garden centres use rooting powder and tissue culture to produce large numbers of identical plants for sale.
Lawn weed killers kill daisies and dandelions without killing the grass.
higherTier: Auxins are used as weed killers, as rooting powders and for promoting growth in tissue culture.
Ethene is used in the food industry to control ripening of fruit during storage and transport.
Gibberellins can be used to end seed dormancy, promote flowering and increase fruit size.
Describe the effects of some plant hormones and the different ways people use them to control plant growth.
separateOnlyContent: This whole subtopic is separate Biology only (8461) and Higher tier only; it is not in Combined Science Trilogy.
examTips: Learn the list exactly: auxins (weed killers, rooting powders, tissue culture), ethene (ripening), gibberellins (dormancy, flowering, fruit size).
When explaining weed killers, link to yield: fewer weeds means less competition for light, water and mineral ions.
For ethene questions, explain why fruit is picked unripe (firm, less damage in transport) and why ripening is controlled (ripe when needed, less waste).
In calculations on yields or success rates, always divide by the original or total value and show your working.
summary: Plant hormones are used to control plant growth in farming and horticulture.
Auxins: selective weed killers, rooting powders, growth in tissue culture.
Ethene: controls ripening of fruit during storage and transport.
Gibberellins: end seed dormancy, promote flowering, increase fruit size.
Using hormones increases yields, produces clones and reduces food waste.

questions.question: Which plant hormone is found in rooting powder?
markScheme: 1 mark: Auxin
questions.explanation: Auxin stimulates roots to grow from the cut end of a cutting. Ethene controls ripening, gibberellins germination, flowering and fruit size; adrenaline is an animal hormone.

questions.question: Which plant hormone is used to control the ripening of fruit during storage and transport?
markScheme: 1 mark: Ethene
questions.explanation: Ethene is a gas that controls ripening, so it can be added or removed to control when fruit ripens.

questions.question: Which of these is a use of gibberellins?
markScheme: 1 mark: Increasing fruit size
questions.explanation: Gibberellins increase fruit size, end seed dormancy and promote flowering. Killing weeds and rooting cuttings use auxins; ripening uses ethene.

questions.question: Selective weed killers contain synthetic versions of which plant hormone?
markScheme: 1 mark: Auxins
questions.explanation: Synthetic auxins cause uncontrolled growth in broad-leaved weeds, which kills them.

questions.question: Why are bananas usually picked before they are ripe?
options: Unripe bananas are firm, so they are less damaged during transport
Bananas can only ripen on the plant
markScheme: 1 mark: Unripe bananas are firm, so they are less damaged during transport
questions.explanation: Firm, unripe fruit bruises less on long journeys. Ripening is then triggered with ethene close to the time of sale.

questions.question: How does a selective weed killer kill broad-leaved weeds?
options: It blocks light from reaching the leaves
It makes the weeds ripen and drop seeds
It causes the weeds to grow rapidly and uncontrollably, so they die
It stops the weed seeds germinating
markScheme: 1 mark: It causes the weeds to grow rapidly and uncontrollably, so they die
questions.explanation: The synthetic auxin disrupts normal growth. The plant cannot sustain the uncontrolled growth, so it dies.

questions.question: Brewers make barley seeds germinate together using a plant hormone. Which hormone, and what does it do?
markScheme: 1 mark: Gibberellins, which end seed dormancy
questions.explanation: Gibberellins initiate germination, so treating seeds with them ends dormancy and makes them germinate at the same time.

questions.question: Why can selective weed killers be used on a field of wheat?
options: Wheat absorbs the weed killer faster than weeds
They kill broad-leaved weeds but not narrow-leaved crops such as wheat
They kill all plants except those planted from seed
markScheme: 1 mark: They kill broad-leaved weeds but not narrow-leaved crops such as wheat
questions.explanation: Narrow-leaved cereals absorb less weed killer, so only the broad-leaved weeds are killed. Wheat does contain auxin naturally.

questions.question: In tissue culture, what are auxins used for?
options: Promoting growth of the small pieces of plant tissue
markScheme: 1 mark: Promoting growth of the small pieces of plant tissue
questions.explanation: Auxins promote the growth of the tissue into new plants (for example, root growth). Sterile technique, not auxin, prevents contamination by microorganisms.

questions.question: Why is rooting powder useful to a plant nursery that wants to sell a rare variety of plant?
options: It makes the plants flower earlier
It allows many identical plants (clones) to be produced quickly from cuttings
It increases the size of the fruit
markScheme: 1 mark: It allows many identical plants (clones) to be produced quickly from cuttings
questions.explanation: Cuttings are clones of the parent, so they keep its desirable features. Auxin helps them root quickly so more survive. Clones are not genetically varied.

questions.question: Apples are stored in cold rooms where ethene is removed from the air. What is the effect?
options: Ripening is slowed, so the apples can be stored for longer
markScheme: 1 mark: Ripening is slowed, so the apples can be stored for longer
questions.explanation: Ethene promotes ripening, so removing it (and keeping the fruit cold) slows ripening. Fruit can then be sold over many months.

questions.question: How can using gibberellins to promote flowering benefit a grower?
options: Plants can be made to flower when conditions would not normally trigger flowering
markScheme: 1 mark: Plants can be made to flower when conditions would not normally trigger flowering
questions.explanation: This lets growers produce flowers (and later fruit) at times of high demand, or in conditions where the plant would not normally flower.

questions.question: Give two uses of auxins in agriculture or horticulture.
markScheme: 1 mark each, any two: as (selective) weed killers; as rooting powders; for promoting growth in tissue culture
questions.explanation: These are the three uses listed in the specification.

questions.question: State three ways that gibberellins can be used.
markScheme: 1 mark: to end seed dormancy
1 mark: to promote flowering
1 mark: to increase fruit size
questions.explanation: These are the three uses of gibberellins listed in the specification.

questions.question: Explain how spraying a crop with a selective weed killer can increase the crop yield.
markScheme: 1 mark: kills (broad-leaved) weeds but not the crop
1 mark: so there is less competition for light, water and mineral ions, so the crop grows better
questions.explanation: Weeds compete with crop plants for the same resources. Removing them gives more resources to the crop.

questions.question: Explain why a gardener might dip the cut end of a cutting in rooting powder before planting it.
markScheme: 1 mark: rooting powder contains auxin, which makes roots grow (quickly)
1 mark: so more cuttings survive / the gardener gets many identical plants quickly
questions.explanation: Without roots, a cutting cannot absorb water and dies. Rapid root growth increases survival.

questions.question: Explain how and why the food industry controls the ripening of fruit such as bananas.
markScheme: 1 mark: fruit is picked unripe because it is firm and less easily damaged in transport
1 mark: ripening is slowed during storage and transport (cool, low ethene)
1 mark: ethene is added to ripen the fruit just before sale, so it is ripe when needed and less is wasted
questions.explanation: Each mark requires a 'how' and a 'why'. Ethene is the key hormone.

questions.question: Seedless grapes are often sprayed with gibberellins. Suggest why.
markScheme: 1 mark: gibberellins increase fruit size
1 mark: larger grapes are more attractive to customers / sell for more / increase yield
questions.explanation: Gibberellins increase fruit size. Bigger fruit gives higher yield and value.

questions.question: Suggest one disadvantage of spraying synthetic auxin weed killers on farmland.
markScheme: 1 mark: may kill non-target plants such as wild flowers (e.g. by spray drift)
1 mark: reducing biodiversity / food sources for insects and other animals (or: cost of chemicals)
questions.explanation: Weed killers cannot distinguish between a weed and a wild flower if both are broad-leaved, so wildlife habitats can be affected.

questions.question: Unripe bananas placed in a paper bag with a ripe banana ripen faster than unripe bananas on their own. Suggest an explanation.
markScheme: 1 mark: the ripe banana releases ethene (gas)
1 mark: the bag traps the ethene, which causes the unripe bananas to ripen
questions.explanation: Ethene is a gas, so it can spread from ripe fruit to nearby unripe fruit. This is the same principle used in commercial ripening rooms.

questions.question: A gardener dipped 40 cuttings in rooting powder. 34 of them grew roots. Calculate the percentage that grew roots.
markScheme: 1 mark: = 85 %

questions.question: Spraying a wheat field with selective weed killer increased the yield from 6.4 tonnes per hectare to 8.0 tonnes per hectare. Calculate the percentage increase in yield.
markScheme: 1 mark: increase = 8.0 − 6.4 = 1.6
questions.explanation: Divide the increase by the original yield. Dividing by 8.0 instead gives 20 %, which is a common error.

questions.question: The mean mass of grapes treated with gibberellins was 7.2 g. The mean mass of untreated grapes was 4.8 g. Calculate the percentage increase in mean mass.
questions.explanation: The untreated mass is the starting value, so it is the denominator. 2.4 ÷ 4.8 = 0.5, which is 50 %.

questions.question: Instructions for a weed killer say: mix 20 cm³ of concentrate with 4 dm³ of water. Calculate the volume of concentrate needed for 30 dm³ of water.
markScheme: 1 mark: 20 ÷ 4 = 5 cm³ per dm³
1 mark: 5 × 30 = 150 cm³
questions.explanation: Find the amount per dm³ first, then scale up. Alternatively 30 ÷ 4 = 7.5, and 7.5 × 20 = 150 cm³.

questions.question: Bananas ripen in 12 days at room temperature without added ethene, but in 5 days in a ripening room with ethene. Calculate the percentage decrease in ripening time. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
markScheme: 1 mark: decrease = 12 − 5 = 7 days
questions.explanation: 7 ÷ 12 = 0.5833, which is 58.3 %. Using 5 as the denominator gives 140 %, which is wrong because the original value is 12.

questions.question: Describe how auxins are used in agriculture and horticulture.
markScheme: Indicative content: synthetic auxins used as selective weed killers; kill broad-leaved weeds by causing rapid, uncontrolled growth; narrow-leaved crops (cereals) unaffected; less competition so higher yield; rooting powders contain auxin; cuttings dipped in rooting powder grow roots quickly; produces many clones of a desirable plant; auxins promote growth in tissue culture; producing many identical plants from small pieces of tissue.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): all three uses described with how or why each is useful.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): uses listed with little description.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: Name each use and add a 'so that' benefit: higher yield, quick rooting, many clones.

questions.question: Farmers, growers and food companies use plant hormones. Describe the uses of auxins, ethene and gibberellins, and explain the benefit of each use.
markScheme: Indicative content, auxins: selective weed killers kill broad-leaved weeds, reducing competition for light, water and mineral ions, so yield increases; rooting powders make cuttings root quickly, producing many clones; promote growth in tissue culture, producing many identical plants.
Ethene: controls ripening of fruit in storage and transport; fruit picked unripe and firm so less damage; ripening slowed then triggered with ethene so fruit is ripe when needed; less waste.

Gibberellins: end seed dormancy so seeds germinate together (e.g. malting barley); promote flowering when conditions would not normally trigger it; increase fruit size (e.g. seedless grapes) for higher yield and value.
Level 3 (5 to 6 marks): uses of all three hormones described, with clear explanations of the benefit of each.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): uses of at least two hormones with some benefits explained.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): some uses named with no explanation.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: Two parts: describe (what) and explain (why it helps). Many answers list uses but miss the benefits, limiting them to Level 2.

questions.question: A company produces banana plants and sells bananas to UK supermarkets. Explain how plant hormones could be used (a) to produce large numbers of new banana plants and (b) to supply ripe bananas to the shops.
markScheme: Indicative content (a): small pieces of tissue from a parent plant with desirable features grown by tissue culture; auxins promote growth of the tissue into new plants; or cuttings treated with rooting powder (auxin) to grow roots quickly; new plants are clones, all with the desirable features; large numbers produced quickly; selective weed killers (auxins) could reduce competition in plantations.

(b): bananas picked unripe and green; firm so less damaged during transport; kept cool with low ethene to slow ripening during shipping and storage; ethene gas added in a ripening room; bananas ripen just before they are needed in shops; reduces waste; allows supply all year.
Level 3 (5 to 6 marks): clear explanations for both parts, naming the correct hormones and linking each use to its benefit.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): correct hormones and uses for both parts with limited explanation, or one part explained well.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): one or two correct uses named.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: Applying knowledge to a new context is typical of grade 7 to 9 questions. Match each stage to the correct hormone: auxins for producing plants, ethene for ripening.
